# Pkl 0.32.0 Class value authority

These fixtures contain actual pinned Java public API observations. No expected bytes come from Rust. The canonical archive retains all raw process stdout/stderr, UTF16BE and Java UTF8 strings, complete logger frames, statuses, actual Java exception/value classes, source/tool snapshots, compile/runtime identities and repeat comparisons.

The main matrix contains 44 source sessions, each in two fresh JVMs. Queries within a session reuse one evaluator and the same module source. It covers canonical runtime Class values, metaclass dispatch, builtin and user superclass relationships, virtual getClass overrides versus intrinsic runtime class lookup, Class<T> erasure, Function0..5, six-parameter rejection, module extends/amends, same names at different URIs, converter specificity, class initialization failure/retry, actual logger reentry/failure/close and UTF16 strings. Every authored query is executed, including intentional negative controls and earlier observed query-scope boundaries. Main call/log/protocol payloads are the common source-query boundary; Java exception class names remain independent producer provenance.

`provider/` records real public Java ModuleKeyFactory.create and ModuleKey.resolve callbacks, including unmatched factory requests. The authored provider is hierarchical, nonglobbable, cached, nonlocal, retains the original URI as resolved URI and performs checkResolveModule. Its protocol records only actual callbacks, with no invented cache events. Candidate provider SPI/API parity remains unexecuted and required unless it is separately mapped and compared. Common query/logger equality does not establish whole session API compatibility.

The separate `exports/` supplement records public evaluateExpression exported-Class reference and equals identity across same URI, changed source, different URI and evaluator instances, plus post-close behavior. Candidate public Class export API parity is unexecuted and required. Returned Java value class names are provenance, not candidate Java-class-name synthesis requirements.

Java converter dispatch is deliberately not generalized: Typed values walk real superclass ancestors; scalar, strict collection, Class and Function values use exact class converters. Any/Number/Collection/Function converters can therefore be ignored for those values. Virtual user getClass() can return String while is and converter dispatch still use the actual user class. User module names beginning pkl. allow an external superclass, but that does not grant permission to declare external members. Same-name user Class values remain distinct from builtins; bare query/type builtin resolution is separately observed.

The archive includes `preserved-history-01/`, `preserved-history-02/` and `preserved-history-03/`: all prior complete acquisitions, including invalid Null(42), local-import/query scope errors and source refinements. They are history, not additional independent feature coverage or candidate passes. Original target captures remain untouched. The final archive uses `main/` and `exports/` for the final authorities.

Run `python3 -B tools/class_values_fixtures.py` to verify offline with no JVM, original target directories, network or subprocess. Independent archive and file-set pins prevent replacing the Java authority by refreshing local manifest hashes. Actual PklBugException and API exceptions remain preserved nonpasses. This is local evidence, not hosted CI, full language/API compatibility, a performance result or completion of M2.
